claims.claim: Ember was 'designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.'
Ember is cheaper and smarter than competitors like Anthropic’s Haiku and OpenAI’s Luna according to Artificial Analysis’s composite benchmark score
At 10 cents per million input tokens, Ember is significantly cheaper than frontier competitors like Haiku and Luna
Ember is cost-competitive with open source competitors like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash
Ember can work from voice memos, meeting recordings, and video without a separate model
Ember is the fourth model released under Meta’s Muse brand, following Spark, Glimmer, and Wonder

delta: supports multimodal inputs (audio, video, images) natively in a lightweight agent-optimized model
priced at $0.10 per million input tokens with lower cost-per-task than Haiku 5.5 despite same token price
achieves higher scores than Haiku and Luna on Artificial Analysis composite benchmarks

prior_art.name: Anthropic Haiku
prior_art.differs: Ember scores same on Intelligence Index (36) but at lower cost-per-task due to fewer output tokens; Ember leads in coding agent benchmarks except FrontierCode 2.0

prior_art.name: OpenAI Luna
prior_art.differs: Ember scores higher than Luna across all reasoning settings and in coding benchmarks (46 vs 31 on Coding Agent Index)

prior_art.name: Muse Wonder
prior_art.differs: Ember is smaller, cheaper, and optimized for repetitive agent tasks, while Wonder is for planning and complex reasoning

tldr: Meta released Muse Ember, a lightweight multimodal API-accessible model at $0.10/million input tokens, independently benchmarked as cheaper per task and stronger in coding than Haiku and Luna.
